text:
oncall-bot: PAGE: perf cliff detected on continuous-batching path for /v1/generate — p95 lat jumped, queue depth spiking, KV cache evictions rising. Paging eng-oncall.
sam: I'm awake, looking at grafana now. Which pools are noisy?
leah: rwd-prod-gpu-1 and rwd-eu-2. Tail latency p95 ~1.2s, normally ~250ms. Token throughput steady though.
devon: KV cache eviction rate jumped 8x starting at 02:04 UTC, aligns with traffic surge. Looks like cache blowback causing microbatch stalls.
sam: Repro: at high concurrency continuous batching seems to create huge microbatch sizes that starve the KV cache and cause long serialization pauses.
elaine: Confirmed on logs: repeated "kv_cache_miss" followed by "microbatch_serialize_timeout" in the runtime.
ops-runner: Customer-facing: several customers (team-alpha, maps-inc) reported timeouts ~02:07-02:12 UTC. CS flagged two upgraded tenants.
leah: Quick check of recent deploys — no new model code; last infra config change was the continuous-batching tweak two days ago that increased max_microbatch_size from 32 -> 256.
devon: That config bump plus a synchronized client burst caused very large microbatches. KV cache size not tuned for that pattern.
sam: Mitigation plan: 1) temporarily cap microbatch size 2) enable jitter on batching to desynchronize 3) fallback route high concurrency to dedicated smaller batch path. I'll run hotfix.
leah: +1. Do we have the admin endpoint to temp-change batching config per pool?
sam: Yep. Using the internal admin API. Command I'm about to run:
```
curl -X POST "https://ops.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools/rwd-prod-gpu-1/config" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"max_microbatch_size": 8, "microbatch_jitter_ms": 25, "enabled": true}}'
```
sam: Pushing to rwd-prod-gpu-1 now.
oncall-bot: Action logged: config-change by sam at 1824501187
sam: Done on rwd-prod-gpu-1. Monitoring.
leah: I'm applying same to rwd-eu-2 with `max_microbatch_size: 4` (safer for EU pool). Doing it now.
devon: Also toggled per-model fallback route for high-concurrency session keys to route to the `continuous_batching_disabled` variant.
elaine: After the first change p95 on rwd-prod-gpu-1 dropped from 1.2s -> 300ms within two minutes. KV evictions back down.
ops-runner: Noted customer impact window: 02:04–02:12 UTC. CS notified impacted customers, working on follow-ups.
sam: We should also add a temporary rate-shedding rule for clients with extreme concurrency to protect the pool while we stabilize.
leah: Agreed — adding a token bucket limiter for per-API-key concurrency > 200. Patch incoming.
devon: Small config diff applied:
```
- continuous_batching.max_microbatch_size: 256
+ continuous_batching.max_microbatch_size: 8
+ continuous_batching.microbatch_jitter_ms: 25
```
sam: Observability: tracer shows reduced queue hold time and fewer serial KV fetch threads. p95 stabilized ~220ms across affected pools.
elaine: I'll open an incident doc and mark as "mitigated, degraded" until we complete root cause and postmortem.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-18245 - Continuous-batching perf cliff (KV-cache contention) — severity 2.
ops-runner: CS draft sent to impacted customers, offering SLA credits where appropriate. Keeping a watch for error spikes.
tariq: I'm next on-call in 40 minutes. Sam/leah, can you DM/summary handoff when you go offline? I'll take watch and runbook.
sam: Will do. Leaving these running notes:
- Root symptoms: high concurrency -> oversized microbatches -> KV cache thrash -> serialization stalls -> latency cliff
- Immediate mitigations: cap microbatch size, add jitter, route to fallback path, apply per-key concurrency limiter
- Short-term next steps: revert max_microbatch_size to conservative default, run load test with synthetic concurrency, increase KV cache capacity if needed
- Long-term: autoscale KV cache memory based on observed microbatch sizes; add circuit-breaker if eviction rate exceeds threshold
leah: Adding runbook snippet in the incident doc now (how to change pool config & where to look in grafana).
sam: Handing off in 20 minutes. I'll keep monitoring for another 10.
tariq: Copy — I'll watch the dashboards and alert if p95>400ms for 5m. Please @mention me for any config rollbacks.
elaine: Postmortem owners: sam (mitigation), leah (config & runbook), devon (runtime changes). I'll assign in ops.
ops-runner: Tagging slack thread for postmortem: #postmortems/inc-2026-18245
sam: One more note: this surfaced during a client-side burst simulator run from an external partner. Recommend we throttle partner traffic or give them a dedicated pool if sustained.
leah: For now, marking incident status as: mitigated → monitoring. Will update incident doc with timeline.
oncall-bot: Incident status changed to "monitoring" at 1824501399
sam: Handoff to tariq: all configs applied, p95 stable, KV evictions down. If you see re-regression, rollback the max_microbatch_size to 4 and disable continuous batching on the pool.
tariq: Got it. Thanks team. I'll take it from here.
